posts.text: The Union of Gaza Municipalities has warned that nearly 1,000 displacement camps and shelters are at risk of flooding this winter, with around 200,000 deteriorating tents in urgent need of replacement and more than 2,000 damaged buildings at risk of collapse. Heavy rainfall in early November damaged around 70,000 tents, affecting more than 350,000 displaced Palestinians. The union called for urgent international intervention, warning that widespread Israeli destruction of infrastructure and continued restrictions on the entry of essential equipment and shelter supplies have severely undermined municipalities’ ability to respond.

Yulia Zhdanova, head of the Russian delegation to the Vienna talks on military security and arms control, said the Dutch authorities could bear responsibility for the actions of staff at Dutch arms maker Destinus, accusing them of carrying out drone strikes from Ukraine against targets in Russia and citing the company’s public acknowledgment that Ukrainian forces used its weapons in the attack on the Crimean Bridge. “Under Article 8 of the UN International Law Commission’s draft articles on state responsibility, the conduct of private individuals may be attributed to a state if they acted on its instructions or under its control,” Zhdanova told a regular plenary meeting of the OSCE Forum for Security Cooperation, according to a text of her remarks obtained by TASS.

The reported activity includes a US Bombardier ARTEMIS II intelligence aircraft and a French Beech King Air 350ER/ALSR surveillance aircraft. Two French Mirage 2000D fighters reportedly departed from Romania, with one using the call sign MIR2 and carrying an ASTAC electronic intelligence pod. A Turkish Navy ATR 72-600 TMPA maritime patrol aircraft is operating over the southwestern Black Sea, while a Turkish Bayraktar TB2 patrols farther south. Meanwhile, a British RAF RC-135W Rivet Joint reportedly departed RAF Waddington to monitor activity around Crimea and Krasnodar. These aircraft movements have not all been independently verified. The concentration of intelligence-gathering aircraft suggests increased attention to Russian military activity around Crimea and the Black Sea. Such missions can help monitor radar emissions, air defense systems, and military movements, providing NATO with a clearer picture of regional threats.
